title: Attributions
lead:
Accurate attribution is essential in the iGEM Competition. It ensures that the judges can properly
assess your team's contributions and recognize the support provided by external collaborators. This page is dedicated to
fulfilling the Attributions requirement for judging.
html:
Bronze Medal Criterion #2

Describe what work your team members did and what other people did for your project using the standardized Project Attributions Form.

Visit the Medals page for more information.

What Should this Page Contain?

  • The standard navigation menu of your wiki
  • The standard footer of your wiki
  • The embedded iframe containing your standardized team's Project Attribution form.
  • Nothing else

Tips for Success

Teams must use the official Attributions form. This form clearly delineates the work conducted by your team members and the support received from others. Carefully review the instructions and requirements of this deliverable on the Project Attribution page. Please note:

  • Teams must use the standard form. Do not create your own form.
  • The standard Attributions Form must be filled out completely, accurately and honestly.
  • For the best results, we recommend teams start filling out the Attributions Form early in the season and updating it often.

Team Members

Aoi Sato

•Investigation: Carried out experiments throughout the project, including E. coli culture and transformation. • Notebook / Record Keeping: Recorded experimental results in the lab notebook. • Project Administration: Coordinated the Wet Lab team’s experiment schedule. • Public Engagement: Took part in educational events in Japan and in events on and off campus. Interviewed stakeholders to gather feedback on real-world implementation. • Writing: Wrote the Application page of the Wiki.

Takumi Kobayashi

• Analysis: Built an image analysis pipeline for experimental images, which made quantitative analysis of the results possible. • Data Curation: Organized experimental results, compared them with the expected outcomes, and considered how to use the findings in the next experiments. • Fundraising: Asked companies for sponsorship and applied for grants. • Public Engagement: Held workshops to share the fun of biology with junior high, high school, and university students. Took part in educational events in Japan and in events on and off campus. Interviewed stakeholders to gather feedback on real-world implementation. • Visualization: Designed posters for events and created visualizations of the Wet Lab results. • Writing: Wrote the Measurement page of the Wiki.

Myléna Seki

• Conceptualization: Helped set the direction of the project and build its early foundations. • Background Research: Reviewed prior research and background on the project ideas to help shape the overall direction. • Public Engagement: Created story content and videos in the early stages of the project. Took part in educational events in Japan and in events on and off campus. Interviewed stakeholders to gather feedback on real-world implementation. • Writing: Wrote the Home and Human Practices pages of the Wiki and proofread the text across the Wiki.

Yuta Watanabe

•Conceptualization: Helped set the direction of the project and shaped the design strategy. •Background Research: Reviewed the existing literature to assess how it applied to the project and whether the project was feasible. •Investigation: Wrote experimental protocols and planned and carried out experiments using E. coli. Established the microscopy observation method. •Data Curation: Organized experimental results, compared them with the expected outcomes, and considered how to use the findings in the next experiments. •Notebook / Record Keeping: Recorded experimental procedures, results, and points for improvement. •Public Engagement: Took part in educational events in Japan and in events on and off campus. Interviewed stakeholders to gather feedback on real-world implementation. •Writing: Wrote the Engineering, Design, Experiments, and Results pages of the Wiki. •Safety: Wrote experimental protocols with safety in mind. Trained members in lab work and submitted the Safety Check-in Form.

Rintaro Taguchi

Interviewed stakeholders to gather feedback on real-world implementation. • Visualization: Edited the Promotion Video. • Writing: Wrote the Description page of the Wiki and proofread the text across the Wiki.

Interviewed stakeholders to gather feedback on real-world implementation. •Visualization: Created visualizations of the coiled-coil structures. •Writing: Wrote the Model-1 page of the Wiki.

External Collaboration Funding •HAZAMA ANDO CORPORATION made a financial donation to support our activities. •Epistra Inc. made a financial donation to support our activities. •Mr. Takayama made a financial donation to support our activities. •Cosmo Bio Co., Ltd. made a financial donation to support our activities.

Materials and Services •New England Biolabs provided reagents for our experiments. •Twist Bioscience provided the genes used in our project free of charge through their free gene synthesis program.

Scientific Advice •Prof. Dr. Dirk Linke, Department of Biosciences, University of Oslo, collaborated with us and gave advice on our experimental design and experiments. •Dr. Hoong Chuin Lim, Principal Investigator, New England Biolabs, collaborated with us and gave advice on our experimental design and experiments. •Prof. Eiji Yamamoto, Department of System Design Engineering, Faculty of Science and Technology, Keio University, advised us on our MD simulations. His advice covered which region of E. coli to simulate, specific simulation methods, and which tools to use. •Dr. Kazufumi Hosoda, Researcher, Center for Information and Neural Networks (CiNet), Advanced ICT Research Institute, National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT), advised us on possible applications of our project.

Team Support •Prof. Junichi Ushiba, Department of Biosciences and Informatics, Faculty of Science and Technology, Keio University, supported the running of our team. •Yagami Innovation Laboratory (YIL), Keio University supported the running of our team. •The staff of YIL, Keio University helped us manage our team's funds. •The Japanese iGEM community advised us on running the team and moving the project forward.

Promotion Video •Ghufron and JULICA helped us produce our Promotion Video.

AI Tools •ChatGPT: Used for writing and proofreading, gathering and organizing information, literature research, brainstorming, coding, and translation. •Claude Code: Used for writing and proofreading, gathering and organizing information, literature research, brainstorming, organizing ideas, coding, writing analysis code, and finding prior research. •Gemini: Used for writing and proofreading, gathering and organizing information, literature research, brainstorming, organizing ideas, coding, exploring analysis methods, and translation. •NotebookLM: Used for gathering information, preliminary paper review, and organizing related literature.
